content: The metabolism of brexpiprazole is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, the dose of brexpiprazole should be reduced to half of the usual dose. If a strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor is also administered, the dose should be further reduced to one-quarter of the usual dose. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, the brigatinib dose should be reduced by 50% (e.g., from 180 mg to 90 mg or from 90 mg to 60 mg). After discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, the brigatinib dose can be resumed to the previously tolerated level. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine transdermal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases cabergoline levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required, the cabozantinib dose should be reduced by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). After discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, the previous dose can be resumed 2–3 days later. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of calcitriol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, the capivasertib dose should be reduced, and the patient should be monitored for adverse effects. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. The use of colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If co-administration is necessary, the colchicine dose or frequency should be reduced as per prescribing information. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, the copanlisib dose should be reduced to 45 mg. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels of eletriptan by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of eluxadoline by reducing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). After discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives, resume the previous encorafenib dose. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Avoid co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of enzalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction accordingly. Erdafitinib increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after administration of P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. Nelfinavir decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, and co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone intranasal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects; monitor for signs/symptoms of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type signs/symptoms. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If such a combination cannot be avoided, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Interrupt and reduce gilteritinib dosage in patients with serious or life-threatening toxicity. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow recommendations for dosage modifications if adverse reactions occur. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of infigratinib (DSC) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg qDay. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose (after at least 5 half-lives of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) to the recommended dose of 500 mg qDay. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used.
